products.description: Arbalette is a serpentine form characteristic of the finest Louis XV commodes and consoles. Our Arbalette chair exhibits a concave center portion with convex edges to form a reverse serpentine shape. The sleek back and arms are often adorned and finished with a nailhead trim. The back legs have a unique shape while the front legs taper to a cylindrical shape.
products.title: Arbalette

products.description: Although the 1930s saw an increasing acceptance of the aesthetics of Modernism, traditional design continued to be dominant. Most people found its references to a settled past reassuring. Our Athens chair adapted from our Neptune Frame recalls the classic form of the Klismos Style. Shown with her splayed front legs and a smart angular back that reaches the height of comfort, our Athens chair is striking in its absolute purity.
products.title: Athens

products.description: Our Aarhus chair is a manifestation of the timeless design of the shield back chair. This frame gives a modern feel to the classic hepplewhite design with its light, slender and curvilinear shape, creating a graceful and delicate appearance.
products.title: Aarhus

products.description: Representative of art in harmony with nature, our Aarhus chair presents sculpted sleek and geometric lines to create a next century feel.  Soothing and yet startling, its unique curves tell the story of this incomparable design.  And yet once seated you won't ever want to leave it. The future is now.
products.title: Aarhus

products.description: The austerity of this chair reflects the ideals of the designer revolution with it's subtle decorative treatment and clean crisp lines. The design and scale of the frame give it universal appeal making it useful with many different decors.

products.description: King George III was still a bachelor when he ascended the throne of Great Britain. He married the seventeen year old Princess Charlotte, the youngest daughter of Duke Charles of Mecklenburg-Strelitz in 1761. In 1762, the new queen gave birth to her first child, the Prince of Wales who would later be known as George IV. Our Charlotte chair is named after the queen who was responsible for the interior decoration of their residence at Windsor. This frame features and boasts a boxed welt design which borders its sides, top, and seat.
products.title: Charlotte

products.description: The 17th and 18th centuries include what is known as the Age of Libraries. The first important library with complete access to the public was Chetham's library in Manchester, England. Our Chetham chair features scroll arms that continue back to form the frame's back legs. It boasts, as standard, a finely executed hand button tufted inside back and a single welt throughout the frame.
products.title: Chetham

products.description: The Delano chair came into being with the youth in mind. In the early 21st century, the youth have emerged as a strong market force that has influenced design. Our frame, which employs arms that synthesize into rear legs, attacks the principles of tradition. The body of the chair boasts more classical elements retaining a geometric design.

products.description: The saying goes there is nothing new under the sun but the function of design is to draw from, reinterpret, and recast the old into the new. Our contemporary Dolce chair draws inspiration from the simple forms of the late 20th century. Working with a gently curved and extended back, we kept things simple yet elegant by ending with a modified Duncan Fiffe leg at the rear, and a gently tapered leg at the front. The armchair is found on the opposite folio.
